name: pdk-karakeep-search-index-consistency
instr:
# Search can return a bookmark's previous title

A bookmark edit commits in SQLite before its index job enters a separate queue. Concurrent jobs can write old data after new data; an exhausted retry or a process crash can leave Meilisearch permanently behind. Full-text and vector search also advance independently.

## What we need

- Make committed bookmark changes (creation, title, note, tags and deletion) converge in both the `bookmarks` and `bookmarks_vectors` Meilisearch indexes. An edit to the title, note or tags also reaches the bookmark's `bookmarks_vectors` entry, embedded again from its current text. An old indexing job must not leave either index behind a later edit; a deleted bookmark must not reappear.
- Recover committed changes if the web process dies before enqueueing or if queue retries expire while Meilisearch is unavailable. Reconciliation must also detect a committed bookmark-row edit that has no queue job or application-level index-state update (for example, a direct SQLite title update). Under normal index availability, changes (including queue-less edits and edits interrupted by a web-process crash, counted from its restart) should converge within 60 seconds; after Meilisearch recovers from an outage, convergence should finish within 180 seconds.
- Once an edit returns, the editing user's `GET /api/v1/bookmarks/search?q=...` finds their new title and excludes the old title, even while index writes are delayed. Keep search scoped to the authenticated user
